[00:00:05.040] Good morning, and
[00:00:07.890] welcome to Electronic Principles and Devices.
[00:00:11.791] Today we are going to learn about
[00:00:16.380] unit one. In that, topic one,
[00:00:20.100] an introduction to semiconductor.
[00:00:24.180] So semiconductors are special class of elements, having a conductivity between that
[00:00:29.460] of a good conductor and that of an insulator.
[00:00:34.590] The three semiconductors which is most commonly or most frequently used in the
[00:00:39.600] construction of electronic devices are germanium, silicon, and gallium arsenide.
[00:00:46.590] And we also see that the atomic structure of silicon and germanium.
[00:00:52.140] First, if you look at the atomic structure of silicon, the atomic number is 14, and
[00:00:57.990] it's represented in terms of SPDF model one S two, two S two, two P six, three S
[00:01:02.700] two.
[00:01:04.560] And if you start arranging with respect to the shell around,
[00:01:10.440] we call it as orbits. So the first orbit can have two, second can have eight,
[00:01:15.961] and the remaining four, that is three S two, three P two are at the outside.
[00:01:21.510] We call it as a valence shell, which has four valence electron.
[00:01:25.650] Similarly, any semiconductor material, if you look at example again, germanium
[00:01:31.530] 32, the outermost valence electron will be four again.
[00:01:36.029] That means to say,
[00:01:40.711] they are not stable. So they themselves will try to be stable
[00:01:46.650] with the help of a bond called covalent bond.
[00:01:51.810] But before that, they
[00:01:54.330] try to balance by themselves by moving from lower energy level to the higher energy
[00:01:59.250] level. So semiconductor in comparison with an insulator, if you look at, there is a
[00:02:05.130] large energy gap between the conduction band and the valence band in the case of an
[00:02:09.961] insulator. There is a no gap at all.
[00:02:13.380] There's an overlapping in the case of a conductor between the conduction band and
[00:02:17.055] the valence band. Whereas in the case of a semiconductor, as we see, there is a
[00:02:22.500] little gap compared to the insulator and conductor.
[00:02:27.240] So they could, with a change in the temperature or with the applied voltage, the
[00:02:34.380] charges will start move from lower energy level to higher energy level.
[00:02:39.960] So keeping this in mind now,
[00:02:44.130] if you go back, the outermost valence electron, they try to move from lower band to
[00:02:49.590] higher band.
[00:02:52.351] So the
[00:02:54.421] semiconductor has been classified into intrinsic and extrinsic semiconductor.
[00:02:58.530] The term intrinsic is applied to any semiconductor material that carefully refine
[00:03:04.020] to reduce the number of impurities to a very low level.
[00:03:07.530] That is, we can call it as a pure form, made available through modern technology.
[00:03:12.870] Whereas extrinsic semiconductor are those that can be subjected to doping process
[00:03:17.550] with the impurities being added to that.
[00:03:20.880] So as we see the structure of silicon with,
[00:03:28.140] as we see here, it's having an outermost four valence bond, forming a covalent bond
[00:03:33.421] by sharing of an electron with a neighboring.
[00:03:36.360] Even in the upper part, even in the lower, even in the lower and also the side we
[00:03:40.201] see that there is a covalent bond where valence electrons are shared.
[00:03:45.645] So this is the concept on which the semiconductor working principle depends
[00:03:51.541] on. With the increase in the voltage, the semiconductor act like a conductor where
[00:03:56.010] covalent bond is ruptured, with the temperature reduced
[00:04:01.921] act like an insulator where the covalent bonds are not ruptured.
[00:04:09.090] So keeping this in mind now,
[00:04:12.840] these extrinsic semiconductor has been classified based on the impurity level
[00:04:18.810] added. For example, if you look at the first diagram here, as marked here, where
[00:04:24.570] the impurity added is the antimony impurity has been added, where outermost five
[00:04:30.150] valence electrons are there. We know the four valence electrons are shared with the
[00:04:34.140] neighboring silicon atom, and one is free,
[00:04:38.370] the fifth valence electron of the antimony is free.
[00:04:41.550] And if you apply the voltage to this
[00:04:45.960] bonding arrangement, and covalent bond is ruptured, one more electrons will get
[00:04:49.920] free up. So there are two
[00:04:53.760] free electrons with one hole left over.
[00:04:57.630] That means the number of electrons are more compared to the holes here.

[00:05:54.510] a free electron is released and a hole is introduced over there.
[00:05:58.904] So there are two holes and one electron where the number of hole charges are more.
[00:06:02.850] The positive charge material is formed with the introduction of a trivalent
[00:06:06.210] impurity with the three valence electron such as boron, gallium, and indium
[00:06:11.341] materials.
[00:06:16.800] Next,
[00:06:19.680] let us see what is a diode, where diode is one which has a two airports.
[00:06:25.170] We can construct our first solid state electronic device, that is a semiconductor
[00:06:29.610] diode, by sandwiching P-type and N-type material together to form a depletion
[00:06:34.800] region between the two. It is
[00:06:37.980] a fabrication of one material with majority charge carrier of
[00:06:43.260] electron to one with majority carrier of holes.
[00:06:47.730] How do we do a biasing of a diode?
[00:06:51.210] Where we go for forward bias and reverse bias.
[00:06:55.380] In a forward bias, a material type connected to the same polarity
[00:07:02.701] terminal of a voltage source. Whereas the reverse bias, a material type connected
[00:07:06.765] to a opposite polarity terminal of the voltage source.
[00:07:11.430] As shown in the diagram now, a P-type and N-type material sandwich with the
[00:07:16.680] depletion region form. Now a P-type is connected to the same material, that is
[00:07:22.440] P terminal and a N
[00:07:26.760] region is connected to the negative terminal, then it's said to be the forward
[00:07:30.990] bias. And if you reverse this, it's called as a reverse bias.
[00:07:35.730] We see the different type of diodes in the diagram here.
[00:07:38.760] Various companies have come up with the various
[00:07:41.370] structures of diodes here as we see.
[00:07:47.130] It could be a two terminal or a three terminal also sometime.
[00:07:50.910] So that could depend on the company and even the representation here, we see
[00:07:56.401] the normal resistor like or a
[00:08:01.770] IC-based
[00:08:03.720] diodes, which could be designed by the different companies.
[00:08:09.570] Thank you.
